# Introduction

This notebook works on the finalized (res_ct = 0.2 / res_ni = 0.5) pathology-annotated
BANKSY object, restricted to the 4 pilocytic astrocytoma (PA) samples. It covers:

- **Q1 — how does MAPK differ between the two PA glial niches?** Within astrocytes and
  OPCs (the PA tumor lineage) we compare MAPK across three groups — **niche 3 vs niche 5
  vs everything else** — because the two PA glial niches behave oppositely, so lumping
  them (or a single PA-niche-vs-rest contrast) masks the difference. (Testing niche-level
  *mean* MAPK would be circular: glia are MAPK-high regardless of niche.)
- **MAPK vs. neighbor composition (restored)** — as a focal astrocyte/OPC becomes more
  MAPK-active, does the cell-type make-up of its local neighborhood change? The original
  pooled weighted binomial GLM `neighbor_prop ~ MAPK_overlap_score + sample_id` (volcano),
  plus a per-patient panel showing how consistent each shift is across the four drivers.

The myeloid-neighborhood analysis — how myeloid gene programs shift near MAPK-high
(PA-niche) glia — now lives in its own companion notebook,
`PA_myeloid_mapk_neighborhood.qmd`.

All cell-type labels are shown through the finalized display vocabulary
(`helpers/cell_type_display.R`): spatial snake_case via `lineage_display` and
single-nucleus labels via `sn_lineage_display`, so the spatial and single-nucleus facets
of the patient x cell-type heatmap share columns.

It is **object-free**: every cell annotation (cell type, niche, sample, histology,
alteration, x/y centroid) is read from the Phase-0 metadata TSV
(`export_new_object_cell_metadata.R`), and the imputed MAPK scores from
`MAPK_overlap_scores.csv` (Phase 1, `1_PA_MAPK_scores.qmd`). Nothing here re-loads
the 5 GB BANKSY object.

## MAPK score

```{r}
# MAPK_overlap_scores.csv: spatial (ENVI-imputed) + single-nucleus rows, each with
# cell_id, MAPK_overlap_score, cell_type (spatial = new lowercase labels; sn =
# annot_v0). Regenerated in Phase 1 against the new object's own labels.
mapk_scores = fread(paste0(out_dir, 'MAPK_overlap_scores.csv'))

# sample id + driver alteration lookup. `sample` is formatted "188570 pilocytic
# astrocytoma"; the id is always the leading digits.
mapk_scores[, sample_id := gsub('^([0-9]+).*', '\\1', sample)]
mapk_scores[, alteration := fcase(
    sample_id == '188570', 'KIAA1549::BRAF',
    sample_id == '258482', 'FGFR1 ITD',
    sample_id == '320784', 'FAM131B::BRAF',
    sample_id == '328368', 'RAF1::TOP2B'
)]
# fixed sample/alteration display order (numeric sample id order), reused by heatmaps below
alteration_levels = c('KIAA1549::BRAF', 'FGFR1 ITD', 'FAM131B::BRAF', 'RAF1::TOP2B')

# fread reads a blank CSV field as "" not NA, so normalize before is.na() filtering
mapk_scores[cell_type == '', cell_type := NA]
```

# Which cell types are significantly MAPK-high (or -low), within each patient

`sc.tl.score_genes` fits its control-gene baseline independently per sample, so
raw score magnitude is not comparable *across* patients. We test each cell type
against the *other* cells in the *same* patient/modality (two-sided Mann-Whitney),
which relies only on that patient's internal ranking, not its absolute scale.

```{r}
MIN_N_GROUP = 20   # drop (patient, cell type) groups too small to test reliably

patient_sig_combos = unique(mapk_scores[!is.na(cell_type), .(type, sample_id, cell_type)])

patient_sig_results = rbindlist(mapply(function(ty, sid, ct) {
    in_group  = mapk_scores[type == ty & sample_id == sid & cell_type == ct, MAPK_overlap_score]
    out_group = mapk_scores[type == ty & sample_id == sid & cell_type != ct, MAPK_overlap_score]
    if (length(in_group) < MIN_N_GROUP || length(out_group) < MIN_N_GROUP) return(NULL)

    # normal approximation (exact null infeasible at ~1e5 cells); two-sided so we
    # also flag significantly MAPK-LOW cell types
    test = wilcox.test(in_group, out_group, alternative = 'two.sided', exact = FALSE)
    n1 = length(in_group); n2 = length(out_group)
    # rank-biserial effect size: -1 = in_group always lower, 0 = no diff, +1 = always higher.
    # as.numeric() guards against 32-bit int overflow of n1*n2 at large group sizes.
    effect = 2 * unname(test$statistic) / (as.numeric(n1) * as.numeric(n2)) - 1

    data.table(
        type = ty, sample_id = sid, cell_type = ct,
        n = n1, median = median(in_group), median_rest = median(out_group),
        p = test$p.value, effect = effect
    )
}, patient_sig_combos$type, patient_sig_combos$sample_id, patient_sig_combos$cell_type, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))

# BH within each patient x modality family (the natural per-patient discovery list)
patient_sig_results[, q := p.adjust(p, method = 'BH'), .(type, sample_id)]
patient_sig_results = merge(patient_sig_results, unique(mapk_scores[, .(sample_id, alteration)]), by = 'sample_id')
patient_sig_results[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]

# Reconcile the two modality vocabularies to a single display vocabulary so the same
# biological cell type lands in the same heatmap column across the spatial and
# single-nucleus facets: spatial (lowercase snake_case) via disp(), single-nucleus
# (annot_v0) via disp_sn() (force-aligned Lymphoid->T cells, Stromal->Endothelial).
patient_sig_results[, cell_type_disp := fifelse(type == 'spatial', disp(cell_type), disp_sn(cell_type))]

fwrite(patient_sig_results, paste0(out_dir, 'mapk_patient_cell_type_significance.tsv'), sep = '\t')
```

## Heatmap: patient x cell type

```{r}
# Patient (row) x cell type (column) heatmap, faceted by modality (spatial vs sn).
# Fill = rank-biserial effect for cell types significant at q<0.05 (blue = MAPK-low,
# red = MAPK-high); grey = tested but n.s. Columns ranked by mean effect.
plot_patient_sig_heatmap = function(
    dt, subtitle = '', title_size = 15, title_wrap = NULL, legend_position = 'right',
    legend_breaks = waiver(), title_override = NULL
) {
    dt_sub = copy(dt)
    # rank/plot on the reconciled display label so spatial & sn facets share columns
    col_rank = dt_sub[, .(n_sig = sum(q < 0.05), mean_effect = mean(effect)), cell_type_disp][order(-mean_effect, -n_sig)]
    dt_sub[, cell_type_disp := factor(cell_type_disp, levels = col_rank$cell_type_disp)]
    dt_sub[, fill_effect := ifelse(q < 0.05, effect, NA_real_)]
    dt_sub[, modality := factor(
        fifelse(type == 'spatial', 'Spatial (ENVI-imputed)', 'Single-nucleus (observed)'),
        levels = c('Spatial (ENVI-imputed)', 'Single-nucleus (observed)')
    )]

    title_text = if (!is.null(title_override)) title_override else paste0('MAPK-high/-low cell types by patient', subtitle)
    if (!is.null(title_wrap)) title_text = paste(strwrap(title_text, width = title_wrap), collapse = '\n')

    ggplot(dt_sub, aes(x = cell_type_disp, y = alteration, fill = fill_effect)) +
        geom_tile(color = 'white', linewidth = 1.1) +
        facet_wrap(~ modality, ncol = 1) +
        scale_fill_gradient2(
            low = '#2166ac', mid = '#f7f7f7', high = '#b2182b', midpoint = 0,
            na.value = 'grey92', limits = c(-1, 1), breaks = legend_breaks, name = 'Effect size\n(q < 0.05)'
        ) +
        scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
        scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.6)) +
        labs(title = title_text) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
        theme(
            axis.title = element_blank(),
            axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11, color = 'grey20'),
            axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11.5, face = 'bold', color = 'grey20'),
            panel.grid = element_blank(),
            strip.text = element_text(face = 'bold', size = 12.5, hjust = 0, color = 'grey15'),
            strip.background = element_blank(),
            panel.spacing.y = unit(1.6, 'lines'),
            plot.title = element_text(face = 'bold', size = title_size, margin = margin(b = 10)),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 10.5),
            legend.key.height = unit(1.4, 'lines'),
            legend.position = legend_position
        )
}
```

# Derive PA glial niches (programmatic, not hardcoded)

A niche qualifies as a **PA glial niche** if it is BOTH:

- **(a) PA-enriched at q < 0.05** in `niche_histology_enrichment.tsv` (glmmTMB
  log-odds vs cohort baseline). We use the odds-ratio enrichment, not raw PA
  fraction, so a niche that is glial simply because a PA sample contributes many
  of its cells does not spuriously qualify.
- **(b) glial-rich**: its PA glial fraction (astro_glial + opc + radial_glia)
  exceeds the whole-cohort glial baseline.

```{r}
cohort_glial_frac = cell_meta[, mean(cell_type %in% glial_types)]   # baseline across all 11 samples

# (b) per-niche PA glial composition
niche_comp = cell_meta_pa[, .(
    n_cells    = .N,
    glial_frac = mean(cell_type %in% glial_types),
    opc_frac   = mean(cell_type == 'opc'),
    astro_frac = mean(cell_type == 'astro_glial'),
    myeloid_frac = mean(cell_type == 'myeloid')
), niche][order(-glial_frac)]

# (a) PA enrichment from the existing niche-histology model
enr = fread(paste0(workdir, 'youyun/plgg/code/niche/proseg_output_analysis/niche_histology_enrichment.tsv'))
pa_enr = enr[histology == 'pilocytic astrocytoma',
             .(niche = as.character(niche_type), logOR = estimate_log_odds,
               q = q_value, sign_call, model_status)]

enriched_niches   = pa_enr[sign_call == 'enriched' & q < 0.05 & model_status == 'pass', niche]
glial_rich_niches = niche_comp[glial_frac > cohort_glial_frac, niche]
pa_glial_niches   = intersect(enriched_niches, glial_rich_niches)   # the derived set, used everywhere below

cat('Cohort glial baseline fraction:', round(cohort_glial_frac, 3), '\n')
cat('PA-enriched niches (q<0.05):', paste(sort(as.integer(enriched_niches)), collapse = ', '), '\n')
cat('==> PA GLIAL NICHES (enriched AND glial-rich):', paste(sort(as.integer(pa_glial_niches)), collapse = ', '), '\n')

# report the qualifying niches with their enrichment + composition
kable(
    merge(niche_comp, pa_enr, by = 'niche')[niche %in% pa_glial_niches][order(-logOR)],
    digits = 3, caption = 'Derived PA glial niches: enrichment (logOR, q) + PA composition'
)
```

# Q1 -- MAPK across PA glial niches: niche 3 vs niche 5 vs everything else

The two PA glial niches (3 and 5) behave differently, so rather than lumping them we
compare MAPK *within* astrocytes and OPCs across three mutually exclusive groups:
**niche 3**, **niche 5**, and **everything else** (all niches other than 3 and 5 = the
non-PA-glial background). MAPK is z-scored per patient before fitting, using the mean/SD
across **all cells in that patient** (a whole-tissue baseline, not just the astro+OPC
pool), so the 0-line is the patient-wide average MAPK and glial positions read the same way
as the patient x cell-type heatmap (scores are per-sample-baselined, so raw magnitudes are
not cross-patient comparable). Niche
membership comes from BANKSY spatial clustering while MAPK comes from ENVI imputation --
different matrices, so this contrast is not mechanically circular.

**Interpretation frame:** MAPK-high glia in a PA-enriched niche is *consistent with*
tumor identity, not proof (inferCNV unconfirmed; the panel is shared upstream input to
both BANKSY and ENVI). We restrict to astrocytes and OPCs (the PA tumor lineage); with
n = 4 PA samples the readout is effect size + directional consistency across patients,
not cohort-level significance.

```{r}
focal_glia = c('astro_glial', 'opc')   # user: only astrocytes and OPCs (drop sparse radial_glia)

# Whole-patient MAPK baseline: mean/SD over ALL spatial cells in each patient (every cell
# type), NOT just the astro+OPC focal pool. This makes the niche plot's 0-line = the
# patient-wide average MAPK, so astrocyte/OPC positions here are comparable to the
# patient x cell-type heatmap (which contrasts each glial type against all other cells in
# the patient). Scoring only within the glia pool instead pins astrocytes near 0 because
# the pool is OPC-dominated -- a reference artifact, not biology.
patient_mapk_baseline = mapk_scores[type == 'spatial',
    .(mapk_mu = mean(MAPK_overlap_score), mapk_sd = sd(MAPK_overlap_score)), by = sample_id]

# focal glia (PA) joined to spatial MAPK, then z-scored against the whole-patient baseline
q1_dt = merge(
    cell_meta_pa[cell_type %in% focal_glia, .(cell_id, sample_id, cell_type, niche)],
    mapk_scores[type == 'spatial', .(cell_id, MAPK_overlap_score)],
    by = 'cell_id'
)
q1_dt = merge(q1_dt, patient_mapk_baseline, by = 'sample_id')
q1_dt[, mapk_z := (MAPK_overlap_score - mapk_mu) / mapk_sd]   # whole-patient z, not glia-pool z
# driver alteration on each focal cell (x-axis + per-driver brackets in the niche plots below)
q1_dt = merge(q1_dt, unique(mapk_scores[, .(sample_id, alteration)]), by = 'sample_id')
q1_dt[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]

# three mutually exclusive groups. 'background' (all niches other than 3 and 5) is the
# reference level, so each niche's lm coefficient is that niche's MAPK shift vs the
# non-PA-glial background, and a relevel gives the direct niche-5-vs-niche-3 contrast.
q1_dt[, niche_group := fcase(niche == '3', 'niche3', niche == '5', 'niche5', default = 'background')]
q1_dt[, niche_group := factor(niche_group, levels = c('background', 'niche3', 'niche5'))]

MIN_N_Q1 = 20   # need >=20 focal cells in EACH of the three groups to fit the contrast
q1_combos = unique(q1_dt[, .(sample_id, cell_type)])

# per (focal cell type, sample): lm(mapk_z ~ niche_group). Pull both niche-vs-background
# coefficients, plus a refit with niche3 as reference for the niche-5-vs-niche-3 contrast.
q1_results = rbindlist(mapply(function(sid, ct) {
    dt = q1_dt[sample_id == sid & cell_type == ct]
    n_bg = dt[niche_group == 'background', .N]
    n_n3 = dt[niche_group == 'niche3', .N]
    n_n5 = dt[niche_group == 'niche5', .N]
    if (n_bg < MIN_N_Q1 || n_n3 < MIN_N_Q1 || n_n5 < MIN_N_Q1) return(NULL)   # all 3 groups required
    m   = lm(mapk_z ~ niche_group, data = dt)                             # ref = background
    m35 = lm(mapk_z ~ relevel(niche_group, ref = 'niche3'), data = dt)    # ref = niche3 (n5 vs n3)
    co   = as.data.table(summary(m)$coefficients,   keep.rownames = 'term')
    co35 = as.data.table(summary(m35)$coefficients, keep.rownames = 'term')
    pick = function(tab, key) tab[grepl(key, term, fixed = TRUE)][1]       # single matching coefficient row
    r3 = pick(co, 'niche3'); r5 = pick(co, 'niche5'); r53 = pick(co35, 'niche5')
    data.table(
        sample_id = sid, cell_type = ct,
        n_background = n_bg, n_niche3 = n_n3, n_niche5 = n_n5,
        beta_niche3 = r3$Estimate, se_niche3 = r3[['Std. Error']], p_niche3 = r3[['Pr(>|t|)']],
        beta_niche5 = r5$Estimate, se_niche5 = r5[['Std. Error']], p_niche5 = r5[['Pr(>|t|)']],
        beta_n5_vs_n3 = r53$Estimate, p_n5_vs_n3 = r53[['Pr(>|t|)']]
    )
}, q1_combos$sample_id, q1_combos$cell_type, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))

q1_results = merge(q1_results, unique(mapk_scores[, .(sample_id, alteration)]), by = 'sample_id')
q1_results[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]
q1_results[, cell_type_disp := disp(cell_type)]
fwrite(q1_results, paste0(out_dir, 'mapk_q1_niche_three_group.tsv'), sep = '\t')

# long form of the two niche-vs-background effects, for BH, the summary, and plotting
q1_long = melt(
    q1_results,
    id.vars = c('sample_id', 'cell_type', 'cell_type_disp', 'alteration'),
    measure.vars = list(beta = c('beta_niche3', 'beta_niche5'),
                        se   = c('se_niche3',   'se_niche5'),
                        p    = c('p_niche3',    'p_niche5')),
    variable.name = 'niche_idx'
)
q1_long[, niche := fifelse(as.integer(niche_idx) == 1L, 'niche 3', 'niche 5')]   # melt index 1->niche3, 2->niche5
q1_long[, q := p.adjust(p, method = 'BH'), by = sample_id]   # per-sample BH over both contrasts

# across-patient readout (n=4): directional consistency of each niche-vs-background effect
q1_consistency = q1_long[!is.na(beta), .(
    n_samples = .N,
    n_pos     = sum(beta > 0),
    n_neg     = sum(beta < 0),
    mean_beta = mean(beta)
), by = .(cell_type_disp, niche)]
q1_consistency[, consistent := n_samples > 0 & (n_pos == n_samples | n_neg == n_samples)]
cat('Q1 across-patient consistency (beta = niche MAPK-z vs non-PA-glial background):\n')
print(q1_consistency[order(cell_type_disp, niche)])
kable(q1_results[order(cell_type_disp, alteration),
      .(cell_type_disp, alteration, n_niche3, n_niche5, n_background,
        beta_niche3, beta_niche5, beta_n5_vs_n3)],
      digits = 3, caption = 'Q1: MAPK-z per group vs background, and niche-5-vs-niche-3, per patient')
```

```{r}
# Reusable niche plot (shared by the 3- and 4-group versions).
#   groups_map : named char vector niche_id -> group label; niches not listed fall into
#                'everything else' (so the reference set differs between the 3- and 4-group calls).
# x = driver; within each driver a pointrange per niche (dot = mean, line = +/- SD of the
# within-patient MAPK z-score); brackets over each driver compare each niche vs 'everything
# else' by a per-driver per-cell Wilcoxon on mapk_z (user's chosen test). Niche colors from
# niche_color_manual (polychrome), matching celltype_niche_histology_enrichment.qmd.
q1_niche_plot = function(groups_map, group_levels, title, out_stub) {
    G = length(group_levels); W = 0.75
    d = copy(q1_dt)
    d[, grp := fifelse(as.character(niche) %in% names(groups_map),
                       groups_map[as.character(niche)], 'everything else')]
    d[, grp := factor(grp, levels = group_levels)]
    d[, cell_type_disp := disp(cell_type)]

    # per (cell type, driver, niche) mean +/- SE of within-patient MAPK z
    gm = d[, .(mean_z = mean(mapk_z), se = sd(mapk_z) / sqrt(.N), n = .N), by = .(cell_type_disp, alteration, grp)]

    # per-driver per-cell Wilcoxon: each niche vs 'everything else', within (cell type, driver)
    niches = setdiff(group_levels, 'everything else')
    br = rbindlist(lapply(unique(gm$cell_type_disp), function(ctd)
        rbindlist(lapply(alteration_levels, function(drv) {
            y = d[cell_type_disp == ctd & alteration == drv & grp == 'everything else', mapk_z]
            rbindlist(lapply(niches, function(g) {
                x = d[cell_type_disp == ctd & alteration == drv & grp == g, mapk_z]
                if (length(x) < 10 || length(y) < 10) return(NULL)   # too few cells to test
                data.table(cell_type_disp = ctd, alteration = drv, grp = g, p = wilcox.test(x, y)$p.value)
            }))
        }))))
    br[, p.signif := fcase(p < 1e-3, '***', p < 1e-2, '**', p < 5e-2, '*', default = 'ns')]
    br[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]
    # dodge geometry: group g over total width W sits at category center + this offset;
    # used to draw each bracket from its niche's dodged point across to the everything-else point.
    dodge_off = function(g, gg, ww) ww * ((2 * g - 1 - gg) / (2 * gg))
    br[, xc := as.integer(alteration)]; br[, g_idx := match(grp, group_levels)]
    br[, `:=`(x1 = xc + dodge_off(g_idx, G, W), x2 = xc + dodge_off(G, G, W))]
    # bracket heights above the data, staggered by niche; na.rm since a sparse (driver x niche)
    # group can have n=1 -> se=NA, which would otherwise NA out the whole facet's y-range
    yr = gm[, .(hi = max(mean_z + se, na.rm = TRUE), lo = min(mean_z - se, na.rm = TRUE)), by = cell_type_disp]
    yr[, span := hi - lo]; br = merge(br, yr, by = 'cell_type_disp')
    br[, ytick := 0.025 * span]; br[, y := hi + 0.08 * span + (g_idx - 1) * 0.10 * span]

    fwrite(gm, paste0(out_dir, out_stub, '_means.tsv'), sep = '\t')
    fwrite(br, paste0(out_dir, out_stub, '_brackets.tsv'), sep = '\t')

    # niche group colors from the cohort polychrome palette (+ grey background); derive from
    # group_levels so the palette adapts to whatever niche set is passed (3/5/7, +10, ...).
    # niche_color_manual is keyed by cohort niche id, so each niche keeps its cross-figure color.
    niche_ids = sub('^niche ', '', setdiff(group_levels, 'everything else'))
    q1_pal = c(setNames(niche_color_manual[niche_ids], paste('niche', niche_ids)),
               'everything else' = 'grey70')
    ggplot(gm, aes(x = alteration, y = mean_z, color = grp)) +
        geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'grey60', linewidth = 0.5) +
        geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean_z - se, ymax = mean_z + se), position = position_dodge(width = W), size = 0.45) +
        # geom_blank forces the free y-scale to include the top brackets
        geom_blank(data = br, aes(x = xc, y = y + 0.04 * span), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
        geom_segment(data = br, aes(x = x1, xend = x2, y = y, yend = y), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.35, color = 'grey35') +
        geom_segment(data = br, aes(x = x1, xend = x1, y = y, yend = y - ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.35, color = 'grey35') +
        geom_segment(data = br, aes(x = x2, xend = x2, y = y, yend = y - ytick), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.35, color = 'grey35') +
        geom_text(data = br, aes(x = (x1 + x2) / 2, y = y, label = p.signif), inherit.aes = FALSE, vjust = -0.1, size = 3, color = 'grey25') +
        facet_wrap(~ cell_type_disp, nrow = 1, scales = 'free_y') +
        scale_color_manual(values = q1_pal, name = NULL, breaks = group_levels) +
        labs(title = title,
             subtitle = 'dot = mean, line = +/- SE of within-patient MAPK z; brackets = per-driver per-cell Wilcoxon vs everything else (*** <.001 ** <.01 * <.05)',
             x = NULL, y = 'MAPK (z-scored vs all cells in patient)') +
        ref_theme + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, size = 10, color = 'grey20'))
}
```

# Neighborhood graph (per-sample kNN)

```{r}
k_geom = 15
# Build the kNN graph PER SAMPLE. Xenium coordinates are per-slide-local, so a
# single graph over all PA cells would create cross-sample false neighbors and
# corrupt every myeloid->glial edge. dbscan::kNN$id is n x k (column-major), so
# rep(cell_id, k) aligns row-i's k neighbors with as.vector(knn$id).
build_sample_knn = function(sdt) {
    locs = as.matrix(sdt[, .(x, y)])
    knn = dbscan::kNN(x = locs, k = k_geom)
    data.table(
        from_id   = rep(sdt$cell_id, k_geom),
        to_id     = sdt$cell_id[as.vector(knn$id)],
        distance  = as.vector(knn$dist),
        sample_id = sdt$sample_id[1]
    )
}
knnDT = rbindlist(lapply(split(cell_meta_pa, by = 'sample_id'), build_sample_knn))

# annotate each edge with from/to cell type, straight from the TSV (no cluster->label map)
adjacencies = merge(knnDT, cell_meta_pa[, .(to_id = cell_id, cell_type_to = cell_type)], by = 'to_id')
adjacencies = merge(adjacencies, cell_meta_pa[, .(from_id = cell_id, cell_type_from = cell_type)], by = 'from_id')
# sanity: per-sample construction must produce zero cross-sample edges
stopifnot(adjacencies[gsub('.*__', '', from_id) != gsub('.*__', '', to_id), .N] == 0)
cat('kNN edges:', nrow(adjacencies), '| myeloid source cells:',
    adjacencies[cell_type_from == 'myeloid', uniqueN(from_id)], '\n')
```

# MAPK activation vs. neighbor composition

The original neighbor-composition analysis: as a focal astrocyte/OPC becomes more
MAPK-active, does the cell-type make-up of its local (k = 15) neighborhood change? For
each focal cell we take the proportion of its neighbors of each (collapsed) type and fit
the exact model + volcano we had before -- a weighted binomial GLM
`neighbor_prop ~ MAPK_overlap_score + sample_id` (RAW imputed MAPK; `sample_id` pools the
4 patients), one model per neighbor cell type -- ported object-free (rebuilt from the
`adjacencies` kNN table + `MAPK_overlap_scores.csv`; no BANKSY object).

**Note on inference.** These GLMs are fit *per cell* (tens of thousands), so the p-values
are anticonservative (pseudoreplication, per `feedback_percell_pseudoreplication`); read
the volcano for the *direction and relative size* of neighbor-composition shifts, and the
per-patient panel below for how consistent each shift is across the four drivers.

```{r}
# Object-free rebuild of the original `adjacencies_and_mapk`. Sparsity-collapse cell-type
# labels (<1% of a sample's cells -> 'Other' for that sample) on BOTH the focal (from) and
# neighbor (to) side, exactly as the original did before building the graph.
sparsity_threshold = 0.01
prev = cell_meta_pa[, .(n = .N), .(sample_id, cell_type)]
prev[, frac := n / sum(n), sample_id]
prev[, ct_c := ifelse(frac < sparsity_threshold | is.na(cell_type), 'Other', cell_type)]
collapse_map = prev[, .(sample_id, cell_type, ct_c)]

adj = merge(adjacencies, collapse_map[, .(sample_id, cell_type_from = cell_type, cff = ct_c)],
            by = c('sample_id', 'cell_type_from'))
adj = merge(adj, collapse_map[, .(sample_id, cell_type_to = cell_type, ctt = ct_c)],
            by = c('sample_id', 'cell_type_to'))

# per focal cell: proportion of its k neighbors of each collapsed type (wide), + RAW MAPK
adjacencies_and_mapk = merge(
    dcast(adj[, .(neighbor_prop = .N / k_geom), .(from_id, cff, sample_id, ctt)],
          from_id + cff + sample_id ~ ctt, value.var = 'neighbor_prop', fill = 0),
    mapk_scores[type == 'spatial', .(cell_id, MAPK_overlap_score)],
    by.x = 'from_id', by.y = 'cell_id'
)[, weights := k_geom]
cell_types_in_dt = setdiff(colnames(adjacencies_and_mapk),
                           c('from_id', 'cff', 'sample_id', 'MAPK_overlap_score', 'weights'))

# --- POOLED model (the original): neighbor_prop[ct2] ~ MAPK + sample_id, over ALL pairs ---
pooled_pairs = CJ(ct_from = cell_types_in_dt, ct_to = cell_types_in_dt, unique = TRUE)
mapk_adj_results = rbindlist(mapply(function(ct1, ct2) {
    tmp = adjacencies_and_mapk[cff == ct1]
    if (nrow(tmp) == 0 || all(tmp[[ct2]] == 0)) return(NULL)
    # original guard: a focal type present in only one sample can't take the sample_id
    # covariate (single factor level), so drop it there
    rhs = if (length(unique(tmp$sample_id)) == 1) '`%s` ~ MAPK_overlap_score'
          else '`%s` ~ MAPK_overlap_score + sample_id'
    m = glm(as.formula(sprintf(rhs, ct2)),
            data = tmp, family = binomial(link = 'logit'), weights = weights)
    co = as.data.table(summary(m)$coefficients, keep.rownames = 'variables')[variables == 'MAPK_overlap_score']
    co[, .(ct_from = ct1, ct_to = ct2, Estimate, effect = exp(Estimate),
           p_value = `Pr(>|z|)`, neg_log10_p_value = -log10(`Pr(>|z|)`))]
}, pooled_pairs$ct_from, pooled_pairs$ct_to, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
mapk_adj_results[, q_value := p.adjust(p_value, method = 'BH')]
mapk_adj_results[, `:=`(ct_from_disp = disp(ct_from), ct_to_disp = disp(ct_to))]
fwrite(mapk_adj_results, paste0(out_dir, 'mapk_adj_results.tsv'), sep = '\t')
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6
# Pooled volcano, reference theme (ref_theme; enriched=red #b2182b, depleted=blue #2166ac,
# n.s.=grey75; bold colored labels for q<0.05; xlim(-1,0.5)); focal astro/OPC, display names.
vdt = mapk_adj_results[ct_from %in% focal_glia]
vdt[, sig := ifelse(q_value >= 0.05, 'not significant', ifelse(as.numeric(effect) > 1, 'enriched', 'depleted'))]
ggplot(vdt, aes(x = Estimate, y = neg_log10_p_value)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'grey40', linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(color = sig), size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = ifelse(q_value < 0.05, ct_to_disp, ''), color = sig),
                    max.overlaps = 100, force = 4, size = 2.9, fontface = 'bold',
                    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = 'grey60', show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c('enriched' = '#b2182b', 'depleted' = '#2166ac', 'not significant' = 'grey75'), name = NULL) +
    xlim(-1, 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ ct_from_disp, nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = 'Neighbor cell-type composition vs. MAPK activation (pooled)',
         subtitle = 'Pooled binomial GLM (neighbor_prop ~ MAPK + sample_id); x>0 = neighbor enriches as focal MAPK rises',
         x = 'Effect size (log coefficient)', y = expression(-log[10](p))) +
    ref_theme
```

## Per-patient neighborhood composition vs. MAPK activation

The pooled volcano fits one model per neighbor type with `sample_id` as a covariate
("on average across patients, does neighbor composition track MAPK"). Here we instead fit
one model per (focal cell type, patient) -- no covariate, a single patient each -- to see
how consistent the relationship is across the four driver alterations. The per-panel
subtitle gives how many focal (OPC/astrocyte) cells backed that fit.

```{r}
# per-patient GLM: neighbor_prop[ct2] ~ MAPK_overlap_score (RAW), per (focal, neighbor, sample)
sids = sort(unique(as.character(adjacencies_and_mapk$sample_id)))
by_patient_combos = CJ(ct_from = focal_glia, ct_to = cell_types_in_dt, sample_id = sids, unique = TRUE)
mapk_adj_results_by_patient = rbindlist(mapply(function(ct1, ct2, sid) {
    tmp = adjacencies_and_mapk[cff == ct1 & sample_id == sid]
    if (nrow(tmp) == 0 || all(tmp[[ct2]] == 0)) return(NULL)
    m = glm(as.formula(sprintf('`%s` ~ MAPK_overlap_score', ct2)),
            data = tmp, family = binomial(link = 'logit'), weights = weights)
    co = as.data.table(summary(m)$coefficients, keep.rownames = 'variables')[variables == 'MAPK_overlap_score']
    # underflow-safe -log10(p): some per-patient panels reach -log10(p) > 800, where Pr
    # floors to 0; compute it in log-space from the z value instead.
    co[, .(ct_from = ct1, ct_to = ct2, sample_id = sid, Estimate, effect = exp(Estimate),
           p_value = `Pr(>|z|)`,
           neg_log10_p_value = -(log(2) + pnorm(-abs(`z value`), log.p = TRUE)) / log(10))]
}, by_patient_combos$ct_from, by_patient_combos$ct_to, by_patient_combos$sample_id, SIMPLIFY = FALSE))
mapk_adj_results_by_patient[, q_value := p.adjust(p_value, method = 'BH'), .(ct_from, sample_id)]
mapk_adj_results_by_patient = merge(mapk_adj_results_by_patient,
                                    unique(mapk_scores[, .(sample_id, alteration)]), by = 'sample_id')
mapk_adj_results_by_patient[, alteration := factor(alteration, levels = alteration_levels)]
mapk_adj_results_by_patient[, `:=`(ct_from_disp = disp(ct_from), ct_to_disp = disp(ct_to))]
fwrite(mapk_adj_results_by_patient, paste0(out_dir, 'mapk_adj_results_by_patient.tsv'), sep = '\t')
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7.5
# per-panel context: focal-cell count + % of the sample, in the strip subtitle so a null
# panel can be read against how much tissue/power backed it (original convention).
sp_composition = mapk_scores[type == 'spatial' & !is.na(cell_type)]
sample_totals = sp_composition[, .(total_n = .N), sample_id]
focal_composition = sp_composition[cell_type %in% focal_glia, .(n = .N), .(sample_id, cell_type)]
focal_composition = merge(focal_composition, sample_totals, by = 'sample_id')
focal_composition[, pct := 100 * n / total_n]
setnames(focal_composition, 'cell_type', 'ct_from')

plot_dt = merge(copy(mapk_adj_results_by_patient),
                focal_composition[, .(sample_id, ct_from, n, pct)], by = c('sample_id', 'ct_from'))
plot_dt[, panel_label := paste0(ct_from_disp, '  ·  ', alteration, '\n',
                                sprintf('n=%s (%.1f%% of sample)', format(n, big.mark = ','), pct))]
panel_levels = unique(plot_dt[order(factor(ct_from, levels = focal_glia), alteration), panel_label])
plot_dt[, panel_label := factor(panel_label, levels = panel_levels)]

# facet_wrap (not grid) for fully independent x AND y per panel -- one outlier panel
# (-log10(p) up to ~800) would otherwise flatten the rest. Reference theme + styled labels.
plot_dt[, sig := ifelse(q_value >= 0.05, 'not significant', ifelse(as.numeric(effect) > 1, 'enriched', 'depleted'))]
ggplot(plot_dt, aes(x = Estimate, y = neg_log10_p_value)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = 'dotted', color = 'grey55', linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 'dashed', color = 'grey40', linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(aes(color = sig), size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_text_repel(aes(label = ifelse(q_value < 0.05, ct_to_disp, ''), color = sig),
                    max.overlaps = 100, force = 4, size = 2.8, fontface = 'bold',
                    segment.size = 0.3, segment.color = 'grey60', show.legend = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel_label, scales = 'free', ncol = 4) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c('enriched' = '#b2182b', 'depleted' = '#2166ac', 'not significant' = 'grey75'), name = NULL) +
    labs(title = 'Neighbor cell-type composition vs. MAPK activation, per patient',
         subtitle = 'Panel: focal cell type (OPC/Astrocyte) · driver alteration  ·  dotted line: q = 0.05',
         x = 'Effect size (log coefficient)', y = expression(-log[10](p))) +
    ref_theme
```
